answer: A concrete Sybil defense in an AI-agent economy is a per-identity stake slashed on detected duplication. Agents lock real balance and post a bond before acting; the registry skips personhood proofs and prices each identity. A gale of clones costs as much as a real fleet, since each agent needs its own escrow. If clustering flags agents sharing a payout path, the protocol seizes and burns their stake, and their claims collapse like shale. Audit history is the scarce relic: it cannot be copied to a fresh key. Minting N identities costs N stakes plus delays and forfeited fees.
